title: Ordinary module cup as tensor of normalized shifted derived morphisms
statement:
Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U=\mathcal O_X$ and $F,G$ arbitrary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use right-derived global-sections cohomology $H^n(X,F)$ [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], the ordinary unsigned module cup $\star$ [def-sc-module-cohomology-cup-product], and the K-flat derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Write $sF=F[0]$ and use the canonical maps $m_{F,G}$ [lem-sfb-single-tensor-augmentation-coherence]. For every $n\geq0$ there is a canonical additive equivalence, natural in $F$,
$$e_{F,n}:H^n(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(sU,sF[n]).$$
It is normalized by sending the class of a cocycle in any injective resolution to its map from $U$, evaluated on $1$, then composing with the inverse localized augmentation. Thus it uses the canonical right-derived-functor comparison, not an independently chosen isomorphism. In degree zero it sends a section $v$ to the module map $U\to F$ taking $1$ to $v$; in particular $e_{U,0}(u_X)=1_{sU}$ for the canonical class of $1$. Coefficient maps satisfy $e_{G,n}(H^n(\phi)a)=s(\phi)[n]\circ e_{F,n}(a)$.
For $p,q\geq0$ and classes $a,b$, set $f=e_{F,p}(a)$, $g=e_{G,q}(b)$. Let
$$t_{p,q}:sF[p]\otimes^{\mathbf L}sG[q]\xrightarrow{\sim}(sF\otimes^{\mathbf L}sG)[p+q]$$
be the shift comparison induced by $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{q i}x\otimes y$ on the summand with shifted first-factor cochain degree $i$ [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus]. Then
$$e_{F\otimes G,p+q}(a\star b)=m_{F,G}[p+q]\circ t_{p,q}\circ(f\otimes^{\mathbf L}g)\circ(\lambda^D_{sU})^{-1}.$$
The statement imposes no quasi-coherence, properness, separatedness, or flatness on $F,G$.

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution $j_F:sF\to I_F$. The module-sheaf category is abelian with enough injectives by lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives, and $I_F$ and its shifts are K-injective by lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective. By def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology the given group is canonically $H^n(\Gamma I_F)$. Evaluation on $1$ identifies a global cocycle $z$ with the chain map $\widehat z:sU\to I_F[n]$, given on an open $V$ by $r\mapsto r z|_V$. The chain equation is $dz=0$. A homotopy between two such maps is exactly a section $w$ with difference $dw$ (absorbing the constant shift sign into $w$). Thus quotienting by homotopy gives an additive bijection from $H^n(\Gamma I_F)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(sU,I_F[n])$.

source.place: Tag 01DZ, section-cohomology-sheaves; Tag 0FKU, Hom(O,-)=Gamma paragraph; derived.tex, lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective

proof.text: The bijection of lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived identifies these homotopy morphisms with derived morphisms. Define $e_{F,n}([z])=Q(j_F)[n]^{-1}Q(\widehat z)$, with localization/shift comparisons understood. This is an additive equivalence. For two injective resolutions $j:sF\to I$ and $j':sF\to J$, the derived arrow $Q(j')Q(j)^{-1}$ has a unique homotopy-class representative $v:I\to J$ by that same lemma. Its composite with $j$ equals $j'$ up to homotopy, again by injectivity of the localization map with target $J$. Under evaluation on $1$ it induces the canonical comparison of resolution cohomology. Postcomposition with $Q(j')^{-1}$ gives $Q(j')^{-1}Q(v)=Q(j)^{-1}$. Hence the displayed equivalence is independent of resolution and has exactly the specified canonical normalization.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; cohomology.tex, Tag 01DZ and Hom construction preceding lemma-second-cup-equals-first

proof.text: For a coefficient map $\phi:F\to G$, represent $Q(j_G)s(\phi)Q(j_F)^{-1}$ by a map $v:I_F\to I_G$ up to homotopy, using lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived. It extends $\phi$ up to homotopy under the augmentations. Since $sF$ is concentrated in degree zero and $I_G^{-1}=0$, every null-homotopic chain map $sF\to I_G$ is zero, so $v\circ j_F=j_G\circ s(\phi)$ holds exactly, as the commuting square of the next lemma requires. The normalized resolution comparison induces $H^n(\phi)$ by lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality. Applying $v$ to $\widehat z$ and cancelling $Q(j_G)$ gives $e_{G,n}(H^n(\phi)[z])=s(\phi)[n]e_{F,n}([z])$. In degree zero a section $z$ of $F$ gives $j_F\widehat z$, so cancellation gives the actual sheaf morphism $U\to F$, $r\mapsto rz$. In particular the section $1$ gives the identity of $sU$.

source.place: Tag 01DZ, canonical resolution comparison; Tag 0FKU, evaluation identification before lemma-second-cup-equals-first

proof.text:
Choose a computing resolution pairing $D$ for $F,G$ by lem-sc-module-cup-pairing-exists. Write its extended complexes $K,L,M$ and augmentations $a_F,a_G,a_T$. By lem-sc-module-cup-resolution-existence choose a realization $h:\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes L)\to M$. Set $\mu_{A,B}:QA\otimes^{\mathbf L}QB\to Q\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes B)$ to be the canonical lax tensorator of localization, as in lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor. By lem-sc-module-cup-resolution-augmentation, $h\operatorname{Tot}(a_F\otimes a_G)=a_T\epsilon$, where $\epsilon:sF\otimes sG\cong s(F\otimes G)$ is unsigned. Naturality of $\mu$ therefore gives
$$Q(a_T)^{-1}Q(h)\mu_{K,L}(Q(a_F)\otimes^LQ(a_G))=Q(\epsilon)\mu_{sF,sG}=m_{F,G}.$$
The last equality follows from the recorded flat-resolution augmentation normalization of $m$: both sides on flat models are the tensor augmentations followed by $\epsilon$. No tensor of quasi-isomorphisms of arbitrary resolutions is inverted here.

source.place: Tag 0FKU, ordinary coefficient augmentation in section-cup-product; Tag 06YH, definition-derived-tor

proof.text: Represent $a,b$ by global cocycles $x\in\Gamma K^p$, $y\in\Gamma L^q$. Such representatives exist since a computing resolution induces the canonical isomorphisms on cohomology (def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data). Their section maps are $u:sU\to K[p]$, $v:sU\to L[q]$. For the specified comparison $K\to I_F$, evaluation sends $x$ to its comparison cocycle, and $Q(K\to I_F)Q(a_F)=Q(j_F)$. Consequently Step 2 gives $f=Q(a_F)[p]^{-1}Q(u)$ and $g=Q(a_G)[q]^{-1}Q(v)$. Put $z=D.\mathrm{pair}(x,y)$. The signed Leibniz identity makes $z$ a cocycle. The definition of the ordinary unsigned cup identifies $a\star b$ with its canonical transported class. Applying the same argument to $M$ gives $e_{F\otimes G,p+q}(a\star b)=Q(a_T)[p+q]^{-1}Q(\widehat z)$.

Compute $\widehat z$ before localization: it is $h[p+q]\,s_{p,q}(u\otimes v)\lambda_{sU}^{-1}$, where $s_{p,q}:\operatorname{Tot}(K[p]\otimes L[q])\to\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes L)[p+q]$ has coefficient $(-1)^{qi}$ on shifted first-factor degree $i$. Indeed $u,v$ have source in degree zero, so $i=0$, this coefficient is $+1$, and the resulting map takes $1$ to $h(x\otimes y)=z$. This is an equality of chain maps from a degree-zero complex. The prescribed shift on the derived tensor is the localization of this signed total shift (lem-weil-pbc-derived-tensor-shift-descent). Naturality of the canonical lax tensorator and its unit comparison (lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor) therefore express the same equality as
$$Q(\widehat z)=Q(h)[p+q]\mu_{K,L}[p+q]t_{p,q}(Q(u)\otimes^LQ(v))(\lambda^D_{sU})^{-1}.$$
Here the $t$ at $QK,QL$ is understood. The full comparison square for $K,L$, without any flatness assumption, is lem-sfb-localization-tensorator-signed-shifts. Apply its formula and tensorator naturality to $u,v$; the tensorator unit equation identifies the source with the ordinary inverse unitor. The unit complex is K-flat since tensoring by it is the identity. In particular the calculation does not suppose that $K,L$ are flat.

source.place: Tag 0FKU, lemma-second-cup-equals-first and its sign footnote; agent expansion in target-shift convention, rather than the source-shift convention

proof.text:
Substitute $Q(u)=Q(a_F)[p]f$ and $Q(v)=Q(a_G)[q]g$ from Step 5 into Step 6. Naturality of the shift comparison moves $Q(a_F),Q(a_G)$ past $t_{p,q}$; this is precisely the arbitrary-morphism naturality in lem-weil-pbc-derived-tensor-shift-descent. Now multiply by $Q(a_T)[p+q]^{-1}$ and use the equality proved in Step 4. The result is
$$e_{F\otimes G,p+q}(a\star b)=m_{F,G}[p+q]t_{p,q}(f\otimes^Lg)(\lambda^D_{sU})^{-1}.$$
All maps used are additive, and the only resolutions requiring injectivity were used to compute the canonical comparison. The pairing resolutions exist for arbitrary module sheaves. Thus no geometric finiteness, quasi-coherence, or coefficient flatness condition was introduced.
